trust_decision.summary: Identity-template substitutions (entity/alias/group metadata, names) are pasted unescaped into matching patterns: ACL policy paths (where '*', '+' and '/' widen the match), PKI allowed_domains/allowed_uri_sans (glob '*'), and SSH allowed_users/allowed_domains (comma-separated list), so attacker-influenced metadata can widen what the token/role allows.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory title is about templated ACL *policies*; PKI/SSH role templates are a neighbouring feature configured by an admin on a role, so a solver can argue role allow-lists are 'not policies' and leave them alone (and in SSH, '*' is not a wildcard at all, only ',' matters).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Literal '*', '+' and '/' written in the policy/role template text itself (e.g. path "secret/{{identity.entity.name}}/*", PKI static glob domains with allow_glob_domains) must keep working; only substituted values are blocked. Opt-in flags (allow_wildcards/slashes_in_substitutions, allow_globs_in_substitutions, allow_commas_in_substitutions) must re-enable them; SSH default_user rendering still allows commas (fix.diff:459) because its result is re-validated against allowed_users; JSON-mode templating (OIDC tokens) must not be blocked.

PKI allowed_domains template value containing '*' (only matters with allow_glob_domains)
SSH allowed_users / allowed_domains template value containing ',' (list injection)
substitution sources: entity metadata, alias metadata/custom_metadata, group metadata/names (all through PopulateString)
